name: Peregrine Mission One

surface_window.note: This mission has no time on the surface.

outcome_note: Launched January 8, 2024 to deliver 5 NASA CLPS science payloads to Sinus Viscositatis. It did not land.

payloads.name: Laser Retroreflector Array
payloads.purpose: Passive retroreflectors that give orbiting or landing spacecraft a precise laser-ranging location marker.

payloads.name: Neutron Spectrometer System
payloads.purpose: Measures the abundance of hydrogen-bearing materials and bulk regolith composition at the landing site.

payloads.name: Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer
payloads.purpose: Radiation monitor measuring the rate of incident radiation on the lunar surface.

payloads.name: Near-Infrared Volatile Spectrometer System
payloads.purpose: Two-channel near-infrared point spectrometer for surface volatiles.

payloads.name: Peregrine Ion-Trap Mass Spectrometer
payloads.organisation: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / ESA
payloads.purpose: Ion-trap mass spectrometer, flown under NASA's commitment to ESA.

sources.title: Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) Deliveries (page updated May 06, 2026)
Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Sinus Viscositatis

notes: The target coordinate is the IAU centre of the named feature, not a published landing point.

site.name: Sinus Viscositatis (feature centre)
site.source_note: The IAU centre of Sinus Viscositatis, used because no landing point is published. It is not a landing point, and numbers here describe the centre of the named feature. No elevation model covers this site: height, slope and terrain are not modelled.

notes: Mission facts are compiled by hand from NASA pages, LROC images and the IAU Gazetteer; every record carries its sources, last read 2026-09-23.
1 of 1 missions have fields no source confirms; they are listed as unconfirmed, never filled in.
Numbers are Sun and Earth geometry at the target over the mission's surface window, not what any lander measured.
1 target(s) lie outside the 80-90 deg S elevation model; there Sun and Earth are computed against a smooth sphere, so terrain could block more.
Where no landing point is published, the target is the IAU centre of the named feature, which is not a landing point.
